newsitem.title: USA: Former WMX CEO gets compensation deal.
newsitem.headline: Former WMX CEO gets compensation deal.

text.p: Phillip Rooney, former Chief Executive Officer for WMX Technologies, will be paid $2.5 million per year through 2002 as part of his severence package with the waste management company, WMX said.
In a proxy filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, WMX said the cash compensation will be in lieu of all salary, bonuses, incentives and other performance-based compensation.

Rooney and his family will continue to participate in all welfare benefit plans generally available to employees and executives of the company and a split-dollar life insurance arrangement will continue.
The compensation and stock option committee accelerated the vesting of all unvested stock options held by Rooney, the filing said.
Rooney resigned on February 18, about a week after his removal was demanded by the investment group controlled by U.S. investor George Soros.

Following Rooney's resignation, the group dropped its proposed nominees to the board, saying it was convinced WMX "will undertake sincere and successful efforts to bring two new, independent members onto the board of directors."
